newsitem.title: New zealand: NZ yield curve flattens at close as bonds rally.
newsitem.headline: NZ yield curve flattens at close as bonds rally.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (JUN) 92.78 (PREV 92.78) 90-DAYS 7.00 (PREV 7.03) 3-YR BONDS (JUN) 92.35 (PREV 92.27) 02/00 7.54 (PREV 7.60)
OVERNIGHT CASH 6.35 PCT (PREV 6.55) US 5-YR 6.64 (PREV 6.80)
* NZ curve flattens as long bonds rally, shorts stay put
* U.S. Treasury rally cited as major reason for NZ strength
* Further rally dependent on more soft U.S. data
New Zealand debt securities held onto their gains at Wednesday's close to finish stronger across the curve in line with U.S. Treasuries.

Dealers said the yield curve's steepening trend of the last fortnight had started to reverse, with the 11/06s in particular taking a strong fillip from the performance of the U.S. following that country's benign first quarter inflation data.
"Most people in this market I would imagine are still positioned for a steepening yield curve, so this has probably upset a few people," one dealer said.
The 06s' yield ended nine basis points down at 7.85 percent following their convincing break below eight percent on Tuesday, while the 02/00s were down six in yield to 7.54 percent.
The mid bonds also took heart from a NZ$100 million three-year eurokiwi issued by Bank Nederlandse Gemeenten overnight, but dealers said the issue had been largely priced into the market.

Key 90-day bank bills ended fairly steady at 7.00 percent, against 7.03 percent at Tuesday's close. The front futures contract was flat at 92.78, and dealers said the big move of the day in the money market was in overnight cash, which dropped to 6.35 percent overnight from its 6.55 percent finish on Tuesday.

A Wellington dealer said that if the U.S. data due over the next couple of weeks was also surprisingly soft the U.S. market, and thereafter New Zealand debt, could put in a further substantial rally as fears of a Federal Reserve rate hike in May would ebb away.
-- Catherine McCaw, Wellington newsroom (64 4) 471 4275
